rows.claim: Published request and agency response; not an appropriation or solicitation.
rows.explanation: Identify a site for and commit to establishing a full - service hospital within or near CB 2 in the rezoning area, including comprehensive maternity and neonatal care. Long Island City's growing residential population requires local, accessible health care infrastructure to meet basic and emergency needs, especially for families.
rows.headline: Provide a new or expanded health care facility
rows.response: OMB supports the agency's position as follows: Agency does not support and cannot accommodate Explanation: NYC Health + Hospitals is currently in the process of modernizing its infrastructure, increasing its capacity and expanding the range of services it offers to better respond to the community’s growing healthcare needs. In order to create a new health care facility, H+H needs to closely coordinate with the State and conduct a community needs assessments to determine its viability. If the results of the assessment are positive, NYC Health + Hospitals will need to create a master plan and seek capital funding. Please note that the cost and effort required to construct a new facility is significant and NYC Health + Hospitals is currently unable to undertake a project of this magnitude due to lack of funding.

rows.claim: Published request and agency response; not an appropriation or solicitation.
rows.explanation: $3.M to complete outdoor space for Adult Behavioral Health on D9 & E11. NYC Health & Hospitals/Elmhurst is one of the largest providers of mental health care in the borough of Queens, and almost 1/3rd of our inpatient beds are reserved for behavioral health patients. We are seeking funds for the construction of two terraces on our 9th & 11th floors. Research has shown that patients with mental health diagnoses experience less anxiety and depressive symptoms and higher levels of 'well-being' when they spend time in natural environments as part of their treatment. It has been suggested that there is a relationship between the outdoor settings and the recovery of psychiatric patients.
rows.headline: Other expense budget request for HHC
rows.response: OMB supports the agency's position as follows: Agency supports but cannot accommodate Explanation: Capital funding has been allocated to the renovation of the behavioral health space, however, the recreation area is not included in the project scope and cannot accomodate at the moment. NYC Health + Hospitals is actively seeking funding opportunities to address the outdoor space need.

rows.claim: Published request and agency response; not an appropriation or solicitation.
rows.explanation: $2.2M for the PET for Nuclear Medicine NYC Health + Hospitals/Elmhurst has incredibly busy volume and demand for our x-ray and radiation oncology services. In 2024, we provided over 91,518 x rays and over 194,000 diagnostic tests, 5% higher than the previous year. Elmhurst currently lacks PET scan technology and we now have to transfer patients to our sister hospital, NYC Health + Hospitals/Queens, in order to receive this critical care. PET/CT scans provide advanced imagery that serves as an effective way to help discover a variety of conditions, including cancer, heart disease and brain disorders. With PET/CT scans, our healthcare providers can make more accurate diagnoses and treatment plans, leading to better outcomes. PET/CT scans are also less invasive and more comfortable for patients. We expect to do 500 procedures in year 1 after acquiring the equipment and ramp up to additional capacity of 1,000 patients a year in year 2.
rows.headline: Other expense budget request for HHC
rows.response: OMB supports the agency's position as follows: Agency supports but cannot accommodate Explanation: This project received some capital funding, however, it is on hold due to a funding shortfall. NYC Health + Hospitals will pursue funding opportunities from various sources to close the funding gap.

rows.explanation: Construct new Hospital and or Urgent Care in Corona/East Elmhurst area. Elmhurst Hospital is the only medical facility in QCB3 area. The hospital serves over a million patients annually. Our area during the pandemic was hit more than any area in the country. The hospital was heroic in saving lives during the health crisis but like many hospitals, was seriously challenged. Our hospital needs to expand its footprint by building on its existing campus or creating an annex in or near East Elmhurst and North Corona. An additional facility is needed without question.

rows.claim: Published request and agency response; not an appropriation or solicitation.
rows.explanation: $5M for the Lobby Renovations We are requesting additional funding to renovate our hospital entranceways and lobbies and make them more environmentally-friendly and energy efficient. We previously received $5.88 M in City Council, NYS, and BP funding for this project. Upon further assessments of the project, there were additional structural needs identified, along with inflationary cost increases. We are nearly complete with the design and ready to go out to bid. The new entryways will be reconfigured to direct patient flow, making it easier to navigate. Wayfinding features will also be added. Each entryway will also have branded information desks, new walls, floors, ceilings, paint and furniture. As a part our goal to be more sustainable, the entrances will incorporate "green" materials and have been designed to minimize heat and cooling loss.

rows.response: OMB supports the agency's position as follows: Agency supports but cannot accommodate Explanation: This project received some capital funding, but has a funding shortfall. NYC Health + Hospitals will pursue funding opportunities from various sources to close the funding gap.

rows.explanation: Elmhurst Hospital is a lvl. 1 trauma center funded by the city, located in the heart of Queens serving a vast number of patients from the borough, and has seen several upgrades and expansions in recent years, with more to come. Being the only city-funded lvl. 1 trauma center within the immediate reach of our communities, it shoulders a significant trauma burden for a sizeable portion of Queens. While neighboring hospitals are either community-level, private or lvl. 2 trauma centers, H+H/Elmhurst faces the challenge of handling a large number of patients with critical injuries. The former St. John's Hospital, which has been closed for close to 20 years, leaves Elmhurst as the only hospital for the residents of S. Elmhurst and its surrounding vicinity.

rows.explanation: Study, locate and fund Tier 2 or 3 Trauma center in CB14. With 30% increase in population scheduled to occur in next 2-3 years,(10,000 units). and nearest Trauma Center, Jamaica Hospital, is appx 10-16 miles away, depending on where you live on the peninsula. The reconstruction of the Van Wyck also adds additional time to reach the center. Therefore, a local facility is vital. The Councilwoman/Majority Whip, has secured some funding in the previous budget. Continued funding is needed.
rows.headline: Other expense budget request for HHC
rows.response: OMB supports the agency's position as follows: Agency supports but cannot accommodate Explanation: The report published by the Far Rockaway Trauma Healthcare Access Task Force (https://rockawaytraumacare.nyc/trauma-center-report-24) recognizes the need for additional studies such as siting and the range of services provided, as well as the need for additional funding beyond what has been allocated, and a sustainable revenue stream for continued operations. These challenges still need to be resolved.
